summary: Several buttons that belong to one decision, joined into a single control.

pairs.dont: Use a ButtonGroup for a setting where one option stays selected.
pairs.do: Use Radio, or a segmented control, when the choice persists.
pairs.why: Nothing in a ButtonGroup stays pressed. If the control has to show which option is current, it is answering a question, not offering actions.

pairs.dont: Join Save, Cancel and Delete because they sit next to each other.
pairs.do: Group actions that are variations of one job — Day, Week, Month.
pairs.why: Joining two buttons says they are the same kind of thing. Cancel and Delete are not, and the shared edge makes the destructive one easier to hit by accident.

pairs.dont: Fill a group with primary buttons so everything competes.
pairs.do: Use Outline or Secondary for a set of peers, and keep primary for a split of one action.
pairs.why: A row of five primary buttons has no hierarchy left to offer. The solid treatment is for a group that is really one action plus its options.

pairs.dont: Leave the group without a name.
pairs.why: Read on their own, the buttons are six labels with nothing to say what they have in common. The group's name is what supplies it.

pairs.dont: Join eight buttons into one bar.
pairs.do: Keep it to a handful, and move the rest behind a menu.
pairs.why: A long joined bar stops reading as a set of choices and starts reading as a toolbar, where the shared edges are just noise.

pairs.dont: Put bare icon buttons in the group and rely on the shape.
pairs.do: Give each an aria-label, and a tooltip if the icon is not obvious.
pairs.why: An icon in a joined bar has no label beside it to borrow meaning from, so the name has to come from the button itself.
